summary: Crane Mountain's 35-ft steel lookout was removed in 1987; its cab was rescued and by October 2024 had moved to a Thurman farm.

facts.design: 35-ft steel Aermotor LS40 tower with an enclosed, glass-sided cab
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1987; only the cab survives, on a farm in Thurman.

visit.trail_note: The cab sits on the Martins' farm in Thurman. The trip report says the public would be able to enter it on nature walks and at two annual events.

events.note: Conservation Commission built a wood fire lookout tower on the summit in September 1911.
A 35-foot steel Aermotor LS-40 tower, bought in 1918, was erected on the summit in March 1919, replacing the wood tower.
J.H. Adams served as fire observer stationed on Crane Mountain.
Observer J.H. Adams broadcast the alarm for a fire on Spruce Mountain, also called Huckleberry Mountain.
Wikipedia says the tower ceased fire lookout operations at the end of the 1970 season.
DEC placed Crane on an inactive list but continued to maintain it, the trip report says.
Tower reactivated during an October 1973 drought; the observer was credited with spotting two fires.
DEC dismantled the tower in December 1987; a helicopter removed the parts, and the cab was set down in a field owned by Robert and Edith Baker.
Cab moved to the Martins' farm in Thurman in time for the Oct. 12 Thurman Fall Farm Tour.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Most sources give 35 ft (Wikipedia, the trip report, the Adirondack Explorer, the 1918 purchase note). The April 1919 Post-Star quoted on the Forest Lookouts page says 40 ft. The story uses 35 ft and says the sources differ.
The Wikipedia infobox says the tower was installed in 1918, but its body and the trip report place the steel tower on the summit in 1919. The story uses 1919.

Wikipedia says lookout operations ended after the 1970 season; the trip report says DEC placed Crane on an inactive list in 1971; the Adirondack Explorer says observers kept watch in 1971. The story reports both.
The 2024 newsletter says Martin's Lumber, the Adirondack Explorer says Martin's Lumberyard, and the trip report says Martin's Tree Farm. The story says the Martins' farm in Thurman.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 2024 relocation is confirmed by the October 2024 newsletter and the 2024 Adirondack Explorer piece. The exact move date is not given. The newsletter's 'about 30 years ago' refers to the Grangers rescuing the cab from scrap, not the move. The trip report page shows no year, only 'Oct 1', so its date is unverified. Height: 35 ft in four sources, 40 ft in the 1919 Post-Star quote; keep 10.7 m. The trip report's 1973 passage dates an observer's two fires to 'the weekend of November 27th' in a North Creek News-Enterprise item dated November 1, 1973. That date is internally inconsistent, so it was not used. The Explorer photo caption mentions a 1982 photo by Ed Burke; no image URL was retrieved. No source describes the summit today. The access level stays unknown.
